steps.evidence: llm-cost estimate --task world-substrate-mechanic-authoring (2026-11-10): 68 calls, median $0.0021 per call, median 11,551 input and 1,574 output tokens, 0% cached. Estimate rules add a few lines to its output; no new call.

cost_basis.cheapest_design: Cheapest design that still does the job: a chance formula written into the rule by the rules writer (p = 0.03 x days since service) costs nothing per run, but the rule language has no arithmetic between two values (docs/plans/ai_judge.md Decided 3), so it would need a language change of its own, and the curve would be the rules writer's guess fixed at build time. Jev costs under $0.001 per 30-day run with the per-run cache (one call per distinct question and inputs), reads only the declared fields, and needs no language arithmetic. Chosen: Jev with the per-run cache (inferred by agent, 2026-11-10). The binding constraint is latency, not cost: 0.43 s mean per Jev call (measured, ~/projects/data/llm_observability.db, 2026-11-10), about 13 s for 30 calls (Q85). For the judge's stopping point, a Jev chance question would cost about 1/50 of the judge's $0.0016 per check; that option is recorded for the judge plan's J5 (Q86), not taken here.

plain_baseline.answer_path: Jev's estimate of a chance (later a pick or an amount) from the world's facts, used by an estimate rule
plain_baseline.when: E1, before the live sawmill run: the same model (Jev) given the whole world state instead of the declared fields, side by side with Jev given the declared fields and gpt-6-luna given the declared fields, on 10 cases; no Jev call is made for planning (Brian's brief, 2026-11-10)

stage_effects.stage: declared reads: Jev shown only the fields the rule declares, not the whole world (E1)
stage_effects.gap: the plain version (whole world) could let unrelated facts or a resident's words move the chance, and makes the cache key the whole world, so nothing is reused; whether declared reads change Jev's answer is untested until E1's comparison (Q83)

stage_effects.stage: per-run cache: one Jev call per distinct question and inputs (E1)
stage_effects.gap: not an answer-quality stage: it removes repeat calls with identical inputs; its effect on cost and time is measured in E1

stage_effects.stage: draw against the estimate instead of using the estimate as the outcome (E1)
stage_effects.gap: used directly, a probability becomes a truth claim (the retired Jev note's anti-pattern, 'P(fire)=0.81 -> fire=true'), so a world fails every day above a threshold and never below it; shown by argument, untested on a run until E1
